concept: Checkbox is a small square key on the case of an appliance with its function printed beside it: you press it, it drops and springs back, and a tick in printing ink appears on its face to say the option is on.

default_to_avoid.pattern: 18px rounded-square checkbox filled blue with a white tick (Material and Bootstrap checkbox)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A coloured fill spends a hue on a selection, which P1 forbids, and a flat square drawn on the page is not a key with height and travel as P3 asks.

default_to_avoid.pattern: checkbox that tells on from off by fill colour alone
default_to_avoid.why_not: P2 and P4 make a state readable as a shape; a colour change alone vanishes for colour-blind readers and in forced colours.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): small keys with their function printed beside them
Braun cassette deck and amplifier fronts of the 1970s: square push keys with an indicator beside each one
apps/lab/checkbox/index.html: tick on the key, key with lamp, latching key

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The key draws at control.check, 24px, while the whole printed row is the label and stands control.md tall, so the target is 44px.

derivation.consequence: press drops height to 0 in 60–70ms, return runs on the material's spring
derivation.form: Pressing anywhere on the row removes the key's elevation.part and moves it by motion.press-travel; release returns it on motion.release.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The on state is a tick in text.primary printing ink on the plastic key face; no orange and no fill colour mark the selection.

derivation.consequence: a lit level uses ink at full step, never orange
derivation.form: The tick and the mixed dash are drawn at the full ink step with the ring stroke width, readable at 4.5:1 on the key.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The printed label sits beside the key on the same line, a gap.lg away, and is part of the native label element.

options.name: tick printed on the key face
key with an indicator lamp beside it
latching key that stays down when on

variants.reason: A shows on, off and mixed as three different shapes on the key itself, so state survives without colour; B puts the state on an 8px lamp too small to read as a shape, and C makes on look like disabled and leaves no travel to show the next press (P3).

root.why: The whole row, key and printed word, is one native label at least 44px tall, so any of it presses the key.

input.why: A native checkbox sits under the key, hidden from sight but focusable, so Space toggles and the state is announced.

key.why: A small square key of matte plastic with the part shadow and a ring edge that holds 3:1 against the body.

mark.why: The mark is drawn in full-step printing ink with the ring stroke, never orange, on the plastic key face.

tick.why: A tick shape says on, so the state can be read with no colour at all and in forced colours.

dash.why: A short dash says mixed, a third shape distinct from the empty key and the tick.

label.why: The printed word uses the label size in regular weight, in ink, beside the key like printing on a case.

hover.why: Hover darkens the key's printed edge one step and never lifts it, because real keys do not rise.

active.why: Pressing the row drops the key by its travel and collapses its shadow underneath it, at once.

checked.why: When the input is checked the tick appears at once on the key, with no animation of the value.

focus-visible.why: Keyboard focus on the hidden input draws the same dark ring around the visible key as on every part.

disabled.why: A disabled key loses its height and fades to half, while its ring edge and mark stay readable.

data-disabled.why: A disabled row shows the not-allowed cursor and its key no longer travels when pressed by a pointer.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the key changes state at once with no travel and no spring return.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the key keeps a system border and the mark uses the text colour, so both survive.

transform.why: The key travels down in 65ms and returns on the spring so a press reads as a physical stroke.

box-shadow.why: The cast shadow collapses with the press and grows back with the return, following the single light.

border-color.why: The edge step on hover fades briefly so the change is a reply to the pointer, not a flash.
